units: <cite ref="Bava Kamma 95b:13">B. Kam. 95ᵇ</cite> <he>שלשה שמין להן הש׳ ומעלין וכ׳</he> there are three persons for whose benefit the value of an improvement is assessed to be payable in money; they are: the share which the first-born has to pay to the plain heir, if the estate has increased in value before division &c.
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 95b:13">Ib.</cite>, a. fr. <he>ש׳ המגיע לכתפים</he>, v. <cite ref="K01379"><he>כַּתָּף</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 95b:4">Ib.</cite> <he>דמי צמרו ושְׁבָחוֹ</he> the original value of his wool and its additional value (through dyeing).
<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Kamma 9:4">Ib. IX, 4</cite>; <cite ref="Ketubot 80a:8">Keth. 80ᵃ</cite>, v. <cite ref="E00266"><he>הוֹצָאָה</he></cite>.
Pes. 27ᵃ, a. e. יש ש׳ עצים בפת the bread contains the benefit derived from the wood used in baking bread, i.e. bread baked by a fire made of forbidden wood (e.g. an ăsherah) is forbidden; a. fr.
<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 16">Num. R. s. 16<sup>13</sup></cite> <he>לא במקום הש׳ וכ׳</he> they built the cities not on the best soil &c., opp. <cite ref="Q01247"><he>פְּסוֹלֶת</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 16:13">Ib.</cite> <he>להודיעך שְׁבָחָהּ של וכ׳</he> to let thee know the superiority of the land of Israel, v. <cite ref="U00096"><he>שָׁבַח</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Eruvin 18b:13">Erub. 18ᵇ</cite> <he>מקצת שבחו של אדם וכ׳</he> you may tell part of a man’s praise in his presence, but not all of it.

<cite ref="Mishnah Pesachim 10:4">Pes. X, 4</cite> <he>מתחיל בגנות ומסיים בש׳</he> you begin (the recitation of the Agadah on the Passover eve) with disgrace (telling of the slavery or idolatry of the ancestors), and close with praise.

<cite ref="Pesachim 117a:6">Ib. 117ᵃ</cite> <he>בעשרה מאמרות של ש׳ וכ׳</he> the Book of Psalms uses ten expressions of praise &c.; <he>גדול … שכולל שם וש׳</he> the highest of all is Halleluiah, because it contains the Name of the Lord and praise.

<cite ref="Kiddushin 33b:15">Kidd. 33ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Exodus 33:8">Ex. XXXIII, 8</cite>) <he>וחד אמר לש׳</he> and one says, they looked after Moses with the purpose of praising him, v. <cite ref="C01076"><he>גְּנַאי</he></cite>; a. fr.—Tosef. Meg. IV (III), 39; <cite ref="Megillah 25b:3">Meg. 25ᵇ</cite> <he>קורין אותו לש׳</he> are in reading changed for a more aesthetic expression, v. <cite ref="C01076"><he>גְּנַאי</he></cite>.—[Tanḥ. Vaëra 9 <he>ומראה שבחן</he>, read: <he>שַׁחֲצוֹ</he>, v. <cite ref="U00689"><he>שַׁחַץ</he> I</cite>.]
